chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Khashab, from Ibn Baqqah, from Mu'adh al-Jawhari, from 'Amr ibn Jumai', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not sit sideways upon the riding animals, and do not take their backs as gathering places.'

key_terms.الدَّوَابِّ: Al-dawabb — riding animals, typically referring to horses, camels, mules, or donkeys used for transportation
key_terms.تَتَوَرَّكُوا: To sit tatawaruk — with both legs hanging over one side of the animal, a posture considered harmful to the animal and undignified
key_terms.مَجَالِسَ: Majalis — plural of majlis, meaning a sitting place, gathering, or social assembly; indicates prolonged or unnecessary stationary use of the animal's back

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about proper conduct when riding animals?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a prohibition from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) against two discourteous behaviors towards riding animals: sitting with both legs hanging on one side (tatawaruk), and using the animal's back as a place for social gatherings and discussions. The guidance reflects Islamic ethics regarding the treatment of animals — they are to be used purposefully for transport, not exploited as leisure platforms. This teaching would have resonated strongly in 7th-century Arabia where camels, horses, and donkeys were central to daily life and travel.
word_analysis: sit sideways (with both legs on one side)

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Khashab, from Ibn Baqah, from Moaz Al Jowhary, from Amro Bin Jumie, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Do not sit upon the animal with both feet hanging on one side, and do not take its back for a meeting place (to hold discussions while sitting upon it)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Khashshab from ibn Baqqah from Mu‘adh al-Jawhariy from ‘Amr ibn Jumay‘ who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You must not sit on the stumper with both legs hanging from one side (causing imbalance) or make its back a meeting place (talking to someone with the stumper halted and kept on hold).”’
